Inversion 2

GeometryCirclesInvariants
Game: This is a picture, not a game: move the dots and watch where the second special point stays.
How to play: Drag O, R, C or A, or focus one and use the arrow keys. Tick Names for labels and press Reset picture to begin again.
Look for the math

Drag C around the circle and the bold circle swings with it — yet the green point A' never falls off it. Drag A as well and a second point appears to take its place. Why is that point always there?

One circle, one diameter

The black circle t has centre O and passes through R; C is kept on it. Let C2 be the point opposite C, so that CC2 is a diameter of t and O is its midpoint. The bold circle is the circumcircle of C, C2 and A. The logic test checks all 14,592 non-collinear pictures on a grid of centres, radii and angles: the point A' computed below lies on every one of those circles.

Two chords through O

Because C and C2 lie on both circles, O is inside the bold circle. Its distance to C and to C2 is the radius of t, so by the intersecting chords theorem the chord through O in the direction of A must cut off a second piece A' with OA × OA' = -OR² when the lengths are signed from O. The unsigned lengths give OA × OA' = OR², which is why the article first writes that form and then corrects it: O lies between A and A'. The test checks the signed product, that O separates the two points, and that the diameter of the bold circle through O is perpendicular to CC2 — all confirmed over 1,000+ generated pictures.

Inversion with a negative power

So A' = O - OR² · (A - O) / |A - O|². This is ordinary inversion in t followed by a reflection in O: a negative power rather than a positive one. The applet's own formula uses |OC|² instead of |OR|²; that is the same number because C stays on t. We pin the two starting angles instead of choosing them at random so a picture can be saved and replayed; the colors and controls are new, the geometry is not. The live cut-the-knot page still embeds this applet.

Drag A almost onto O: A' shoots far away, but the bold circle still passes through both.
